statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits at 13 of 100 in the low band, twelve points below the 25 block threshold, while stress remains extreme at 86 and confidence is high at 89.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The named danger window covers the August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC on 11 September, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC Michigan preliminary release, where the conditional path peaks at WATCH without reaching the block threshold.
headline: Two and a half hours of post-reopen trade show a probe to 29,062.50 bought back rather than extended: NQ holds 29,112.50, down 0.08%, and tail eases to 13, while a 4.944% ten-year, VIX 17.84 and crude above $103 keep stress extreme at 86 into the August consumer price report.
body:
The overnight price path is the cleanest evidence available and it argues against a pathological regime. CME equity futures have been open for roughly two and a half hours since the 21:00 to 22:00 UTC maintenance halt. NQ trades 29,112.50, down 22.75 points or 0.08% against the 29,135.25 reference, inside a band of 29,062.50 to 29,157.50. That is 95 points, about 0.33%. The session low was set below the 29,098.75 low that stood at the previous assessment, and it was bought back inside the same hour rather than becoming a lower shelf. Price now sits mid-band. A probe that is retraced, not extended, is the single most informative structure for a mean-reversion book, and it is why tail eases another point to 13.

The macro backdrop is the opposite of the price path and it is what keeps stress at 86. Thursday was the fourth consecutive lower cash close: the NASDAQ-100 settled 29,103.51, down 1.08%, with the S&P 500 off 0.58% and the Dow down 0.6%. The ten-year yield sits at 4.944%, up 10.7 basis points on the session and the highest since October 2023, with an intraday high of 4.952% that puts 5% within a single session's range. WTI trades near $103.10 after settling at $102.48, up 6.7%, and Brent settled at $107.63, up 5.9%. Volatility repriced with it: VIX closed 17.84, up 8.38%, its day range 16.29 to 18.17. Beneath the index, the latest session shows semiconductors as the weak leg, with Micron down 4.9%, Intel down 5.6%, Arm down 3.8% and Nvidia down 2.4%, while Apple gained 3.6% and Oracle rose after reporting cloud infrastructure revenue up 121% and remaining performance obligations of $664 billion. That dispersion is a stress signature, not a one-way trend signature.

The energy channel is geopolitical rather than cyclical. U.S. forces struck five tankers linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guard on 8 September, Iran fired ballistic missiles toward U.S. positions in Jordan, and Houthi strikes hit Saudi oil facilities. Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen to roughly ten vessels a day against a pre-war average near 130. That leaves the oil-to-yields-to-multiple chain unusually sensitive to a single headline, which is an unscheduled route to a directional leg and is reflected in stress rather than in tail.

The named checkpoint is the August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC. Consensus centres near 3.3% year over year headline and 2.4% core, and the report is the last inflation reading before the 15 to 16 September FOMC, where futures were pricing roughly 60% odds of a rate increase as of Thursday. Under the standing rule, a Tier-1 event and wide forecast dispersion raise stress and lower confidence before the print rather than raising tail; hypothetical post-release alignment is not counted as observed structure. The conditional path therefore peaks at 23 in the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots, inside the watch band, and eases back through the New York afternoon on the assumption that discovery is orderly. The forward window closes inside the CME weekend halt that begins at 21:00 UTC on 11 September.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 00:00 UTC to 23:00 UTC on 10 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 8 and holds a tight 8 to 11 band through the U.S. overnight, the Asian session and the European morning, with the dominant mode recorded as mixed throughout. The regime change sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the August producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and the window peak of 24 at 13:00 UTC covering post-release discovery and the cash open. Those two slots are the only ones mapped to WATCH; every other hour mapped to EA_ON. Tail then fell back to 17 at 14:00 UTC and 14 at 15:00 UTC as retracements returned, drifted up to 19 into the 20:00 UTC cash close as the oil-led selloff completed a fourth consecutive lower finish, and eased to 15 and then 14 across the maintenance halt and the reopen. Stress rose almost monotonically across the day, from 80 at the open of the window to 87 at the close, tracking crude through $100 and the ten-year toward 5%. Confidence held between 84 and 89 throughout, its two lowest readings sitting in the release hours where forward dispersion was widest.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens with roughly two and a half hours of observed post-reopen trade on 11 September and ends inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC the same day. Conditional tail starts at 13, holds 13 through the first Asian hour and settles at a 12 floor across the thinnest Asian and pre-European hours, where no U.S. macro is scheduled. From the European pre-market it rebuilds gradually, 13 through 14, reaching 16 in the final full hour before the release as quoted depth thins. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot containing the August consumer price report and 23 again at 13:00 UTC, where post-release discovery overlaps the 13:30 UTC cash open, then 20 at 14:00 UTC alongside the Michigan preliminary release. Those three slots are the only ones that map to WATCH; the peak stays two points below the 25 block threshold because the repeated pattern after this week's releases has been a violent but two-sided first reaction rather than a sustained no-retracement leg. From 15:00 UTC the conditional path decays through 18, 16 and 15 on the assumption that volatility subsides and retracements return, lifts to 17 in the 20:00 UTC cash-close hour on weekly rebalancing and weekend headline risk, and falls to 12 and then 11 once futures stop trading. Stress peaks at 92 across the two release hours and never leaves the extreme band. Confidence bottoms at 82 in those same hours and again at 83 inside the closure, where evidence age rather than market condition is the binding constraint.
